newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana president's widow appointed prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Guyana president's widow appointed prime minister.

text.p: Janet Jagan, widow of former Guyanese President Cheddi Jagan, has been appointed prime minister and will be sworn in on Monday as the first woman to hold the office, government officials said.
Jagan, 76, was also appointed first vice-president and is expected to lead her late husband's People's Progressive Party (PPP) in presidential elections later this year, party sources said.

The appointment of Jagan, who will be the country's first foreign-born prime minister, came just nine days after Cheddi Jagan died of heart failure at the Walter Reed hospital in Washington. He was 78.
More than one in four of the 800,000 population of the former British colony in South America came to view Cheddi Jagan's body lie in state before last Thursday's cremation.
Janet Jagan, born in Chicago in 1920, told Reuters she had needed little persuading to accept her new post. "I saw there was a need at this particular time," she said.
A U.S.-trained nurse, she came to Guyana, then British Guiana, in 1943 and has been extensively involved in the country's politics.

As first deputy speaker of the House of Assembly she held several ministerial posts in PPP governments under British rule and was imprisoned for six months following the suspension of the Constitution and ouster of the government in 1955. She is still a member of parliament.

President Samuel Hinds, the former prime minister who was sworn in to lead the country following Jagan's death, said he made the appointment after consultation with Cabinet colleagues and PPP leaders.
